### Module 03 — Survival Analysis (Kaplan-Meier & Log-Rank)

# Survival Analysis (Kaplan-Meier & Log-Rank)

***
**Learning objectives**
- Understand censoring and the survival analysis framework
- Estimate and plot Kaplan-Meier survival curves with confidence bands
- Compare survival curves with the log-rank test and Wilcoxon test
- Compute and interpret median survival time and restricted mean survival
- Stratify survival by clinical subgroups and annotate at-risk tables

**Estimated time:** 2 hours | **Level:** Intermediate | **Libraries:** `survival`, `survminer`, `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `broom`

## 1. Setup & Survival Dataset

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(tibble)
library(patchwork)

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

mod03_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "mod03")
dir.create(mod03_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

logistic <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))

# ── Synthetic survival dataset: time to 30-day readmission ───────────────────
set.seed(42)
N <- 1500
base <- matrix(rnorm(N * 3), ncol = 3)

set.seed(99)
diabetes      <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.6 * base[, 1] - 0.5))
heart_failure <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.4 * base[, 2] - 1.2))
copd          <- rbinom(N, 1, logistic(0.5 * base[, 3] - 1.0))
payers        <- sample(
  c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay"),
  N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.42, 0.22, 0.28, 0.08)
)
ages     <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rnorm(N, 62, 16), 18), 95))
sexes    <- sample(c("M", "F"), N, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.48, 0.52))
los_days <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rgamma(N, shape = 2.5, scale = 1.8), 1), 30))

# Time to readmission (days after discharge, max follow-up = 365)
# Shorter time for patients with HF, diabetes, high LOS
hazard <- exp(-3.5 + 0.5 * heart_failure + 0.3 * diabetes + 0.15 * (los_days > 7) + 0.2 * copd)
time_to_event <- as.integer(pmin(pmax(rexp(N, rate = hazard), 1), 365))

# Censoring: some patients lost to follow-up before 365 days (30% censored)
censor_time <- as.integer(round(runif(N, 30, 365)))
observed    <- as.integer(time_to_event <= censor_time)   # 1 = event observed
duration    <- ifelse(observed == 1, time_to_event, censor_time)

df <- tibble(
  patient_id      = sprintf("PT-%05d", seq_len(N)),
  age             = ages,
  sex             = sexes,
  payer           = payers,
  los_days        = los_days,
  diabetes        = diabetes,
  heart_failure   = heart_failure,
  copd            = copd,
  duration_days   = duration,
  event_observed  = observed
) |>
  mutate(
    age_group = cut(age, breaks = c(17, 44, 64, 74, 95),
                    labels = c("18-44", "45-64", "65-74", "75+")),
    high_risk = as.integer(heart_failure == 1 | diabetes == 1)
  )

cat(sprintf("Survival dataset: %d x %d\n", nrow(df), ncol(df)))
cat(sprintf("Event rate (readmission observed): %.1f%%\n", mean(df$event_observed) * 100))
cat(sprintf("Censoring rate               : %.1f%%\n", (1 - mean(df$event_observed)) * 100))
cat(sprintf("Median follow-up time        : %.0f days\n", median(df$duration_days)))
print(summary(df |> select(duration_days, event_observed)))
```

## 2. The Censoring Concept

> **Censoring** occurs when the event has not yet happened by the end of follow-up, or when a patient is lost. The censored observation still contributes information: we know the patient was event-free up to their last contact.

| Censoring type | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Right-censored | Event not yet occurred at study end | Patient still alive at end of follow-up |
| Left-censored | Event occurred before first observation | Readmission before first clinic visit |
| Interval-censored | Event occurred between two observations | Only know readmission was between visits |

In most clinical registry analyses, **right-censoring** is the norm.

```{r}
# Visualise the censoring structure for a small sample
set.seed(0)
sample_df <- df |>
  slice_sample(n = 25) |>
  arrange(duration_days) |>
  mutate(
    y = row_number(),
    status = if_else(event_observed == 1, "Event (readmission)", "Censored")
  )

p_cens <- ggplot(sample_df, aes(y = y, colour = status)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = duration_days, yend = y), linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(x = duration_days, shape = status), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Event (readmission)" = "#DC2626", "Censored" = "#2563EB")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Event (readmission)" = 4, "Censored" = 16)) +
  labs(
    x = "Days post-discharge", y = "Patient (sample of 25)",
    title = "Patient follow-up timelines — events vs censored observations",
    colour = NULL, shape = NULL
  )

print(p_cens)
ggsave(file.path(mod03_dir, "censoring_diagram.png"), p_cens,
       width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 120)
```

## 3. Kaplan-Meier Estimator — Overall Cohort

```{r}
km_all <- survfit(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ 1, data = df)
med <- as.numeric(surv_median(km_all)$median)

p_km <- ggsurvplot(
  km_all, data = df, conf.int = TRUE, palette = "#1E3A8A",
  xlab = "Days post-discharge", ylab = "Readmission-free probability S(t)",
  title = "Kaplan-Meier survival curve — overall cohort",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal(), legend = "none"
)
p_km$plot <- p_km$plot +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, colour = "#DC2626", linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = med, colour = "#DC2626", linetype = "dotted") +
  annotate("text", x = med + 15, y = 0.52, label = sprintf("Median = %.0f days", med),
           colour = "#DC2626", size = 3.2, hjust = 0) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05))

# Cumulative incidence (1 - S(t))
km_sum <- broom::tidy(km_all)
p_cif <- ggplot(km_sum, aes(time, 1 - estimate)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = 1 - conf.high, ymax = 1 - conf.low), fill = "#DC2626", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_step(colour = "#DC2626", linewidth = 1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05)) +
  labs(
    x = "Days post-discharge", y = "Cumulative readmission probability F(t)",
    title = "Cumulative incidence of readmission"
  )

p_overall <- p_km$plot + p_cif
print(p_overall)
ggsave(file.path(mod03_dir, "km_overall.png"), p_overall,
       width = 14, height = 5, dpi = 120)

# Survival probabilities at key time points
cat("Survival probabilities:\n")
for (t in c(30, 60, 90, 180, 365)) {
  sm <- summary(km_all, times = t, extend = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("  S(%3d days) = %.3f  → %.1f%% readmitted by day %d\n",
              t, sm$surv, (1 - sm$surv) * 100, t))
}
cat(sprintf("\nMedian survival time: %.0f days (50%% readmitted by this day)\n", med))
```

## 4. Stratified KM Curves & Log-Rank Test

```{r}
df <- df |>
  mutate(
    hf_lab = factor(heart_failure, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("0 - No HF", "1 - Heart failure")),
    dm_lab = factor(diabetes,      levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("0 - No DM", "1 - Diabetes"))
  )

km_hf <- survfit(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ hf_lab, data = df)
km_dm <- survfit(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ dm_lab, data = df)
lr_hf <- survdiff(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ heart_failure, data = df)
lr_dm <- survdiff(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ diabetes, data = df)
p_lr_hf <- 1 - pchisq(lr_hf$chisq, length(lr_hf$n) - 1)
p_lr_dm <- 1 - pchisq(lr_dm$chisq, length(lr_dm$n) - 1)

p_hf <- ggsurvplot(
  km_hf, data = df, conf.int = TRUE, palette = c("#2563EB", "#DC2626"),
  xlab = "Days post-discharge", ylab = "Readmission-free S(t)",
  title = "Time to readmission by Heart Failure status",
  legend.title = "", ggtheme = theme_minimal()
)
p_hf$plot <- p_hf$plot +
  annotate("label", x = Inf, y = 0.15, hjust = 1.05,
           label = sprintf("Log-rank p = %.4f", p_lr_hf), size = 3.5) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05))

p_dm <- ggsurvplot(
  km_dm, data = df, conf.int = TRUE, palette = c("#16A34A", "#7C3AED"),
  xlab = "Days post-discharge", ylab = "Readmission-free S(t)",
  title = "Time to readmission by Diabetes status",
  legend.title = "", ggtheme = theme_minimal()
)
p_dm$plot <- p_dm$plot +
  annotate("label", x = Inf, y = 0.15, hjust = 1.05,
           label = sprintf("Log-rank p = %.4f", p_lr_dm), size = 3.5) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05))

p_strat <- p_hf$plot + p_dm$plot
print(p_strat)
ggsave(file.path(mod03_dir, "km_stratified.png"), p_strat,
       width = 14, height = 5, dpi = 120)

# Cox PH as the regression analogue of the log-rank test
cox_fit <- coxph(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ heart_failure + diabetes + copd, data = df)
cat("\nCox proportional hazards model:\n")
print(broom::tidy(cox_fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE))
```

## 5. Multi-Group Comparison (>2 Groups)

```{r}
df$payer <- factor(df$payer, levels = c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private", "Self-pay"))
km_payer <- survfit(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ payer, data = df)
mlr <- survdiff(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ payer, data = df)
p_mlr <- 1 - pchisq(mlr$chisq, length(mlr$n) - 1)

p_pay <- ggsurvplot(
  km_payer, data = df, conf.int = FALSE,
  palette = c("#1E3A8A", "#DC2626", "#16A34A", "#7C3AED"),
  xlab = "Days post-discharge", ylab = "Readmission-free probability S(t)",
  title = "Kaplan-Meier curves by payer type",
  legend.title = "Payer", ggtheme = theme_minimal()
)
p_pay$plot <- p_pay$plot +
  annotate("label", x = Inf, y = 0.15, hjust = 1.05,
           label = sprintf("Multi-group log-rank p = %.4f", p_mlr), size = 3.5) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05))

print(p_pay)
ggsave(file.path(mod03_dir, "km_payer.png"), p_pay$plot,
       width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 120)

# Median survival by payer
cat("Median readmission-free survival by payer:\n")
print(surv_median(km_payer))
```

## 6. At-Risk Table & Restricted Mean Survival Time

```{r}
km_hf_rt <- survfit(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ hf_lab, data = df)

p_atrisk <- ggsurvplot(
  km_hf_rt, data = df, conf.int = TRUE, risk.table = TRUE,
  palette = c("#2563EB", "#DC2626"),
  break.time.by = 30,
  xlab = "Days post-discharge (at-risk counts below axis)",
  ylab = "Readmission-free probability S(t)",
  title = "KM curves with at-risk table — Heart failure subgroups",
  legend.title = "", ggtheme = theme_minimal(),
  tables.height = 0.25
)
print(p_atrisk)
p_atrisk_comb <- p_atrisk$plot / p_atrisk$table + patchwork::plot_layout(heights = c(3, 1))
ggsave(file.path(mod03_dir, "km_atrisk.png"), p_atrisk_comb,
       width = 11, height = 6, dpi = 120)

# Restricted mean survival time (RMST) up to t* = 180 days
rmst_from_survfit <- function(fit, t_max = 180) {
  sm <- summary(fit, times = seq(0, t_max, by = 1), extend = TRUE)
  times <- sm$time
  surv  <- sm$surv
  if (min(times) > 0) {
    times <- c(0, times)
    surv  <- c(1, surv)
  }
  if (max(times) < t_max) {
    times <- c(times, t_max)
    surv  <- c(surv, tail(surv, 1))
  }
  sum(diff(times) * head(surv, -1))
}

fit_hf1 <- survfit(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ 1, data = df |> filter(heart_failure == 1))
fit_hf0 <- survfit(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ 1, data = df |> filter(heart_failure == 0))
rmst_hf1 <- rmst_from_survfit(fit_hf1, 180)
rmst_hf0 <- rmst_from_survfit(fit_hf0, 180)
cat("Restricted Mean Survival Time (RMST) up to 180 days:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Heart failure : %.1f days readmission-free\n", rmst_hf1))
cat(sprintf("  No HF         : %.1f days readmission-free\n", rmst_hf0))
cat(sprintf("  RMST diff     : %.1f days advantage for no-HF group\n", rmst_hf0 - rmst_hf1))
```

## 7. Interpreting Crossing Survival Curves

```{r}
# Simulate crossing curves — when log-rank may be misleading
set.seed(33)
n_cross <- 500
# Group A: early-risk high, late-risk low
t_A <- pmin(pmax(rexp(n_cross, rate = 1 / 60), 1), 365)
e_A <- rbinom(n_cross, 1, 0.65)
# Group B: early-risk low, late-risk high (crossing pattern)
t_B <- c(
  pmin(pmax(rexp(n_cross / 2, rate = 1 / 200), 1), 180),
  pmin(pmax(rexp(n_cross / 2, rate = 1 / 40), 181), 365)
)
e_B <- rbinom(n_cross, 1, 0.60)

cross_df <- tibble(
  time  = c(t_A, t_B),
  event = c(e_A, e_B),
  group = factor(rep(c("Group A (early risk)", "Group B (late risk)"), each = n_cross))
)
km_cross <- survfit(Surv(time, event) ~ group, data = cross_df)
lr_cross <- survdiff(Surv(time, event) ~ group, data = cross_df)
# Wilcoxon (Breslow / Gehan) weighted log-rank — more power for early differences
wilcox_cross <- survdiff(Surv(time, event) ~ group, data = cross_df, rho = 1)
p_lr <- 1 - pchisq(lr_cross$chisq, 1)
p_w  <- 1 - pchisq(wilcox_cross$chisq, 1)

p_cross <- ggsurvplot(
  km_cross, data = cross_df, conf.int = TRUE,
  palette = c("#DC2626", "#2563EB"),
  xlab = "Days", ylab = "S(t)",
  title = "Crossing survival curves — log-rank test loses power\nConsider Wilcoxon (Breslow) test or weighted log-rank",
  legend.title = "", ggtheme = theme_minimal()
)
p_cross$plot <- p_cross$plot +
  annotate("label", x = Inf, y = 0.18, hjust = 1.05, size = 3.2,
           label = sprintf("Log-rank p = %.4f\nWilcoxon p = %.4f\n(may miss crossing)", p_lr, p_w)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1.05))

print(p_cross)
ggsave(file.path(mod03_dir, "km_crossing.png"), p_cross$plot,
       width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 120)
```

## 8. Knowledge Check
1. A patient who withdraws from the study on day 45 without experiencing the event — how should they be coded (duration, event_observed)?
2. The log-rank p-value for HF vs no-HF is <0.001. Is this sufficient to conclude HF causes faster readmission? What is missing?
3. RMST for HF group = 94 days vs no-HF = 131 days. How would you phrase this for a clinical report?
4. When would you prefer Wilcoxon (Breslow) over the log-rank test?
5. Replicate the payer analysis restricted to patients aged 65+ only. Does the ranking of median survival times change?

```{r}
# Exercise 5 — KM by payer for 65+ only
df_65 <- df |> filter(age >= 65)
km_65 <- survfit(Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ payer, data = df_65)
print(surv_median(km_65))
for (pay in c("Medicare", "Medicaid", "Private")) {
  n_pay <- sum(df_65$payer == pay)
  if (n_pay < 20) next
  med_p <- surv_median(survfit(
    Surv(duration_days, event_observed) ~ 1,
    data = df_65 |> filter(payer == pay)
  ))$median
  cat(sprintf("  %-12s (65+): median = %.0f days, N=%d\n", pay, med_p, n_pay))
}

p_65 <- ggsurvplot(
  km_65, data = df_65, conf.int = FALSE,
  palette = c("#1E3A8A", "#DC2626", "#16A34A", "#7C3AED"),
  xlab = "Days", ylab = "S(t)",
  title = "KM by payer — patients aged 65+ only",
  legend.title = "Payer", ggtheme = theme_minimal()
)
print(p_65)
```
